function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieve the current weather conditions for a specified location in either Celsius or Fahrenheit. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to retrieve the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' or 'New York, NY'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the temperature.

function.name: search_local_docs
function.description: Searches the local knowledge base for documents that match the given natural language query and returns relevant document entries. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search query expressed in natural language, such as 'What are the symptoms of a cold?'.

limit.description: The maximum number of documents to return.

include_metadata.description: Determines whether to include metadata for the documents in the search results.

**First Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year** | Award year | Winning film | Release year | |------------|--------------|--------------| | **1998** | *Princess Mononoke* (Japanese title: “Mononoke-hime”) | 1997 | *Princess Mononoke* was the first Ghibli feature to receive the Japan Academy Film Prize’s top honor, beating out other strong contenders such as *The Last Emperor* and *Kagemusha* that year. --- ### How its box‑office success boosted Ghibli’s international popularity | Domestic impact | International impact | |-----------------|----------------------| | • Grossed **¥1.5 billion** (≈ US$12 million) in Japan – the highest‑grossing Ghibli film at the time.
• Became the highest‑grossing Japanese animated film of 1997, cementing Ghibli’s status as a domestic powerhouse.
• The film’s critical acclaim (winning Best Animation, Best Director, etc.) raised the studio’s prestige among Japanese critics and audiences alike. | • Distributed worldwide by **Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures** (under the “Disney–Ghibli” label).
• Earned **US$13 million** worldwide, including significant revenue from the U.S., Canada, and European markets.
• The film’s success proved that Ghibli’s storytelling could resonate beyond Japan, encouraging major distributors to license more Ghibli titles for overseas release. | | **Strategic outcomes** | | | • Ghibli secured a long‑term partnership with Disney for the distribution of its films in North America and parts of Europe.
• The partnership gave Ghibli access to Disney’s marketing machinery, leading to broader promotion of subsequent releases such as *My Neighbor Totoro* (1999) and *Spirited Away* (2001).
• The financial gains from *Princess Mononoke*’s domestic run enabled Ghibli to invest in higher‑budget projects and to launch its own distribution arm, Ghibli Distribution, in 2000. | • The film’s international box‑office performance helped justify the creation of the Ghibli Museum in Mitaka, Tokyo (opened 2001), which further promoted the studio’s brand worldwide.
• The success of *Princess Mononoke* laid the groundwork for the studio’s eventual expansion into merchandising, theme‑park attractions, and licensing agreements with foreign partners. | | **Legacy** | | | • *Princess Mononoke* remains one of the most‑watched Ghibli films in Japan, and its legacy continues to attract new generations of fans.
• The film’s worldwide reach set a precedent for Ghibli’s future releases, making it easier for the studio to secure distribution deals in markets such as the U.K., France, Germany, and South Korea. | • The film’s success demonstrated that Ghibli’s unique blend of environmental themes, complex characters, and high‑quality animation could appeal to adult audiences abroad, broadening the studio’s demographic reach. | In short, *Princess Mononoke*’s domestic box‑office triumph and its successful partnership with Disney for overseas distribution were pivotal in turning Studio Ghibli from a respected Japanese studio into a globally recognized brand. The film’s performance opened doors for future releases, helped the studio secure better distribution deals, and ultimately contributed to the worldwide cult following that Ghibli enjoys today.
